analyst_view.overall: Nottingham Forest (17th, 9 pts, out of the drop zone only on goal difference) host Chelsea (8th, 16 pts) on Friday night, and both lost last weekend: Forest 2-0 at Bournemouth with one shot on target from 17, Chelsea 4-1 at home to Leeds to boos. Forest boss Oliver Glasner said his side must be 'more physical' and is under pressure from owner Evangelos Marinakis again after the win over Manchester City bought him time; Callum Hudson-Odoi and Nicolas Dominguez are out, and Xaver Schlager (hamstring) and Neco Williams (ankle) were doubts last week. Xabi Alonso called Chelsea 'fragile': striker Joao Pedro (thigh), Reece James (knee), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) and Jorrel Hato (back) are out, and Moises Caicedo went off early against Leeds with a back knock and is a doubt. The site's numbers list no missing players for either side, so none of these absences are counted directly, although Joao Pedro, James and Lacroix have already missed recent games that the momentum figures include. No referee is named yet; neither side is in Europe, so there is no midweek rotation.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 1.4 each. I lean slightly lower to about 2.7: Chelsea are without their main striker Joao Pedro until about January (Evening Standard and ESPN), which the numbers don't list, and Forest managed one shot on target at Bournemouth. The lean stays small because Chelsea's recent scoring, part of it without Pedro, is already in the numbers, and their defence (20 conceded in 11) is leaky.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 4.9 each. Forest have been winning a few more corners than usual and Chelsea fewer, and the numbers already move both for that. Without Reece James Chelsea lose some of their crossing from the right, but he has been out for weeks, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Glasner wants Forest 'more physical' in a relegation scrap, which points up, but Caicedo, Chelsea's most frequent fouler in midfield, may miss out, which points down; the numbers already lift Forest for Chelsea drawing cards lately (+11.6%) and cut Chelsea for their own quieter run. No referee is named yet, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, with Forest expected to shoot more (14.7) after 99 shots in their last six games, which the numbers already count (+12.8%). If Caicedo misses out Chelsea's midfield gets weaker and Forest could see more of the ball, but that is not confirmed, so I stay at 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Forest have been shooting a lot but landing few on target (one from 17 at Bournemouth), while Chelsea have been hitting the target fairly often, and the numbers already weigh both. Losing Joao Pedro trims Chelsea a little, but I already took that off goals, so I stay at 8.6.
